roles.title: Senior UX Designer
roles.lede: UX design on a shared services team, with 3 to 12 month engagements across the business.

metric.c: monthly revenue increase from the award-winning OptumRx mobile app in its first quarter, with month-over-month growth after.

probes: Why did it win an award?

Launched in 2014,  the new OptumRx app won the Silver A’ Design Award for accessibility in the "differently abled users" category: prescription renewal and refill time dropped from minutes to under 30 seconds, significantly helping elderly and disabled people.
Any startup work?
Lead designer for Harken Health, a UHC-funded experimental startup.
Legacy systems?
Redesigned green-screen claims processing software and led in-lab usability test planning and facilitation.

roles.title: Staff Designer, Research Lead
roles.lede: Staff designer and dedicated UX researcher for agency clients, and a Design Thinking coach for corporate teams.

metric.c: beta testers recruited from a UX booth at a global conference, learning the goals and challenges of two merging organizations. The follow-up 90-minute workshop was top-rated.

probes: What was the merger?
Led discovery for the Calabrio and Teleopti merger, including product research and user journey mapping.
Field research?
Facilitated a day-in-the-life research study at a Capital One call center.
Coaching?
Coached corporate teams through a 3-day Design Thinking bootcamp.
How did the booth become a pilot group?
Over 3 days, 85 people (over 10% of attendees) signed up to join my client’s ongoing pilot group, so the team had regular access to real users after the conference.

roles.title: Creative Director, Design Systems

metric.c: component libraries consolidated into Netra, the organization’s first multi-themed, token-driven design system, built into the Enterprise Clinical Platform so teams could build micro-products on their own.

probes: How big was the team?
Hired and led 5 UI product designers and mentored 25+ federated designers.
What happened in 2020?
Enabled the launch of UnitedHealth’s first virtual care platform during the COVID-19 shutdown.
How did it stay healthy?
Established a governance and contribution model to keep quality high at scale.
Did people use it?
Drove enterprise-wide adoption, improving brand cohesion, accessibility and consistency.

roles.title: Founding Product Designer

metric.c: clients retained through contract renewal in year one, driven by day-one value from the flagship feature.

Designed the MVP platform, interviewed clients and launched feature sets to beta testers.

Created and launched the Prima Design System.
What did the practice look like?

roles.title: Principal Product Designer

metric.c: in revenue gained by one of the first 8 beta clients from Live Claims Monitoring, the flagship tool I designed.

I manage the design lead and oversee end-to-end UX/UI for the platform.
Where does AI come in?
Integrating agentic experiences that help practitioners manage revenue and better serve their patients.

Setting design direction on core feature sets during discovery, in close collaboration with the Director of Product and VP.

roles.title: Prima DS: a design system built for AI-speed prototyping
roles.lede: I built a startup's design system from zero and turned it into the foundation that let anyone in the company prototype on-brand, with AI tools, in a single session.
roles.hint: Role: Founding Product Designer · Owner of Prima DS · Partners: engineering, product, leadership

metric.c: 0-to-1 systems thinking, design-to-code fluency, and leading AI adoption in a design org.

probes: The Challenge

Aroris was moving fast on the Aroris360 healthcare revenue platform, but every new feature was designed from scratch. Screens drifted visually, engineers rebuilt the same components, and the digital brand looked early-stage to the clinicians we were asking to trust us with their reimbursement data. As AI and vibe-coding tools spread across the company, non-designers began generating UI too, with no shared system to keep it consistent.
Design Approach
I built Prima DS from zero (Figma libraries, semantic tokens tied to code, governance) and made it usable inside AI and vibe-coding tools.
The Impact

• Cut ideation-to-solution from four working sessions to one.
• Accelerated prototyping and time to market for new features across the platform.
• Gave Aroris a consistent, mature digital brand at the moment it began selling to larger practices.
• Made design a company-wide capability: anyone could prototype a credible concept without waiting on a designer.

1.alt: Prima DS color ramps, data visualization and icon foundations

2.alt: Prima DS components in the Negotiation Strategy screens on laptop and tablet

roles.title: Agentic workflows clinicians can trust
roles.lede: I turned an email-and-phone service into an agent-assisted platform, with human checkpoints that kept AI output accurate enough for healthcare revenue decisions.
roles.hint: Role: Founding Product Designer · Partners: PM, AI engineer, data analysts, internal negotiators, beta customers

metric.c: Designing for AI uncertainty, trust and safety in a regulated domain, and shipping in stages with real users.

probes: The Challenge

Aroris helps practices negotiate better reimbursement rates with payers. The service ran offline: analysts cleaned client data in spreadsheets, and negotiators built proposals by hand over email and phone. It did not scale, and clients had no visibility into progress. Adding AI could speed it up, but a wrong inference on a contract or a leaked piece of patient data (PHI) was not an acceptable failure.
Design Approach
I designed agent-assisted data cleanup and a Proposal Modeler, with PHI checks and human-in-the-loop checkpoints, released from alpha to beta to GA.
The Impact

• The AI-assisted cleanup workflow ran about 4x faster than the manual process on its first test run.
• Moved the service from offline interactions to a self-serve, end-to-end platform used by internal teams and “DIY” client users.
• Staged releases caught issues with real users before general availability, protecting trust with paying customers.

0.alt: PHI check flagging restricted columns before data cleanup continues

1.alt: Human-in-the-loop review of AI-assigned provider credentials
The Proposal Modeler analyzing contract and market trends

2.alt: Live Claims Monitoring and AI-generated proposal strategies

roles.title: Internal scalers: from 3 weeks to 3 minutes
roles.lede: By designing tools for our own analysts first, we cut client file digitization from three weeks to under three minutes and gave the admin team back a full workday every week.
roles.hint: Role: Founding Product Designer · Partners: data analysts, customer success, sales, engineering

metric.c: Service design thinking, operational ROI, and a lean build-measure-learn rhythm.

probes: The Challenge

A startup only scales if its internal operations do. At Aroris, onboarding a client meant digitizing contracts, claims and fee schedules by hand in offline spreadsheets. It took weeks, tied up analysts, and delayed the moment clients saw value. Customer success and sales had similar manual work, and none of it was visible in the product.
Design Approach
I designed internal tools first, tested them on real client work, then shipped them to customers, along with widgets like CPT Code Lookup.
The Impact

• File digitization dropped from 3 weeks to under 3 minutes.
• Freed the admin team 8 to 16 hours per week.
• Shipped new product features twice a month.
• Internal tools became customer-facing features, so every operational win also grew the product.

1.alt: Fee schedule analysis widgets with market data

2.alt: The Negotiation Strategy screen used by internal teams and clients

roles.title: Modernizing Apple's supplier platform
roles.lede: I brought consistency to a set of heavily used legacy supply chain tools at Apple and redesigned how Apple and its B2B partners communicate.
roles.hint: Role: Senior Product Designer (consultant via Bitovi) · Partners: supply chain leadership, product, engineering

metric.c: Design systems at enterprise scale, B2B collaboration tools, and credibility with senior stakeholders.

probes: The Challenge

SupplierCare and the Partner Portal connect Apple with the suppliers and partners in its global supply chain. Years of independent feature work had left the tools inconsistent, and each team made its own UI decisions. Partners had no clear way to ask for help; support happened in scattered emails. Documents for programs and broadcasts lived in folder structures that were hard to navigate.
Design Approach
I created a SupplierCare design playbook and component toolkit, and designed “Ask Apple” chat and Pin Boards for the Partner Portal.
The Impact

• Gave the team a single source of truth for UI decisions across heavily used legacy systems.
• Created a direct support channel between Apple and its partners.
• Earned praise from Apple stakeholders: “strong UI/design suggestions and mindset” (Global Head of Partner and Supply Chain Integration) and “great quality of work… navigating a demanding environment” (Worldwide Operations).

1.alt: SupplierCare tables built with the component toolkit

2.alt: Ask Apple chat and Pin Boards in the Partner Portal

roles.title: Replacing InDesign with a purpose-built label tool
roles.lede: I designed an internal app that let Apple's designers build product and shipping labels in a structured UI, with live syncing, approvals and send-to-factory built in, instead of InDesign.
roles.hint: Role: Senior Product Designer · Partners: internal label designers, operations, engineering

metric.c: Designing complex professional tools, replacing entrenched software, and working inside operational constraints.

probes: The Challenge

Apple's product and shipping labels were made in InDesign. That meant manual file handoffs, no single source of truth for label data, and approvals and factory delivery handled outside the tool. At Apple's volume, every manual step was a chance for a costly error on a physical product.
Design Approach
I designed a structured label builder with formatting panels, live data syncing, approvals and send-to-factory in one flow.
The Impact

• Set the path to retire InDesign from the label workflow.
• Gave Apple one system for creating, approving and sending labels to factories.

1.alt: IOR section formatting panel with size, position and scale controls

2.alt: The label build canvas with approvals and send-to-factory

roles.title: Netra: unifying Optum's clinical design system
roles.lede: I led a team that replaced 20 fragmented component libraries with one clinical design system. Within two years, 25+ internal platform teams were building with it.
roles.hint: Role: Creative Director, UX/UI · Managed 5 UX/UI designers · Partners: product leaders, engineering, platform teams

metric.c: Org-level design leadership, managing and growing designers, driving adoption, and enterprise procurement.

probes: The Challenge

Optum's clinical products drew on two sister brands, Optum (orange) and UnitedHealthcare (blue). Teams had built about 20 separate component libraries, which diluted the brand, duplicated effort and made accessibility inconsistent. There was no enterprise Figma license, so designers couldn't share a single source of truth.
Design Approach
I led five designers to build Netra, with tokens, switchable themes, dark mode and accessibility, and secured an enterprise Figma license.
The Impact

• 20 legacy component libraries decommissioned.
• 25+ internal platform teams building with Netra, including an enterprise telehealth and virtual-visit platform.
• 5-star rating for the Netra onboarding experience.
• One token change could now update every product at once.

1.alt: A dark mode clinical screen built with Netra
A designer’s quote about the Netra asset libraries

roles.title: Designing for speed in Target's call center
roles.lede: I surveyed 500+ service agents and used what they told me to design an in-house tool that replaced a vendor product and was built for speed.
roles.hint: Role: Senior UX Designer, eCommerce guest service · Partners: product, engineering, service operations, agents

metric.c: Research at scale, designing for expert users, and spotting improvements outside the brief.

probes: The Challenge

Target's guest service agents worked in a third-party vendor tool for post-order calls and chats. Target wanted to phase it out by moving all of its functions into its own service tool, which had to mature by Q1 of the following year. The risk was clear: if the new tool slowed agents down, wait times and guest satisfaction would suffer.
Design Approach
I surveyed 500+ agents (44.8% ranked efficiency first), mapped returns flows, and designed persistent profiles, new search and multi-session controls.
The Impact

• Gave Target a research-backed design for retiring the vendor tool, built on agents' own priorities.
• Designed for the top need, efficiency, with fewer screen hops and safer multitasking.

0.alt: Returns process map for a guest who received a damaged item

1.alt: Survey results: 44.8% of agents ranked efficiency first

2.alt: Proposed flow: pause promo emails until the order confirmation is sent

roles.title: Mayo Clinic Continuous Care: remote monitoring at home
roles.lede: I designed a companion app that let patients manage chronic conditions from home with connected devices, so nurses no longer had to travel for routine wellness checks.
roles.hint: Role: UX/UI Design Principal (consulting) · Partners: clinical teams, product, brand and social media

metric.c: Accessible healthcare UX for non-technical users, connected-device flows, and brand-to-product craft.

probes: The Challenge

Mayo Clinic was launching remote patient monitoring for conditions such as diabetes. Patients needed to check in daily and share readings from scales, glucometers and heart-rate devices. Clinicians needed that data to arrive reliably. Many users were older or new to apps, and Mayo was mid-rebrand, moving to a new black-and-white, serif-led identity.
Design Approach
I designed a care loop of onboarding, daily check-ins, one-tap device syncing and care team views, in the new brand language.
The Impact

• Nurses no longer had to travel to patients' homes for routine wellness checks.
• Patients gained autonomy and privacy in managing their conditions proactively at home.
• Delivered one of the first digital products in Mayo's new brand language.
